items.title: Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 Switch 2 Port in the Works, Sandfall Warns of Technical Challenge
items.summary: Sandfall is exploring a Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 Switch 2 port but calls it a "big technical challenge", with Unreal Engine 5 features that don't run on the console.
items.content:
Sandfall Interactive is exploring a Nintendo Switch 2 version of Clair Obscur: Expedition 33, but the studio has been candid that getting the Unreal Engine 5 game running on Nintendo’s hardware is a “big technical challenge” with no announcement close. Speaking to Automaton , the team laid out exactly what stands in the way, and it is as much about the size of the studio as the power of the console.

The honest answer, from CEO and creative director Guillaume Broche, is that nothing is settled.

The problem starts with what the game is. “It’s a big technical challenge because we tried to do something beautiful with the game, but of course, the Switch 2 is not as powerful as the PlayStation or the Xbox Series X ,” said Tom Guillermin, Sandfall’s chief technical officer and lead programmer. “So, it’s an important thing for us to consider, especially given the size of our studio.” Guillermin noted that a number of Unreal Engine 5 features simply “don’t work on Switch 2”.

That last point is the crux, because it means the timeline is not fully in Sandfall’s hands. “Epic is introducing features like Lumen Lite now, which is easier to run than the standard Lumen, but these things take time to roll out, so we’ll have to consider the updates coming from Unreal Engine to determine what to do,” said lead character artist Alan Reynaud. In other words, how feasible the port becomes depends on what Epic ships and when.

On timing, Broche was direct. “We are interested in looking for a way to do it, but it’s too early for us to announce anything at this point.”

The studio-size caveat carries weight. Clair Obscur was built by a team of around 30 people with outsourced support, and it went on to sell a million copies in three days and take Game of the Year honours. Sandfall’s position is that staying small is a feature rather than a constraint to grow out of.

Unreal Engine is central to how that works. “For starters, Unreal Engine has all the tools you need to make a game that looks big, even if you’re not a big team,” the team said, crediting fortunate timing as Unreal Engine 5, MetaHuman, Nanite and Lumen each arrived at useful points in production. Blueprints, Unreal’s visual scripting system, matter most: with only four programmers on staff, every game designer and technical artist uses Blueprints to build game and environment logic, which the studio calls crucial to shipping at that quality. The same dependency that let 30 people make something that looks enormous is what now ties a Switch 2 port to Epic’s roadmap.

Read More: Clair Obscur Expedition 33 Future Teased As Writer Refuses To Reveal Plans

Sandfall’s reluctance to scale up is deliberate, and Broche frames the game’s constraints as part of why it worked. The studio operates out of a Montpellier building it calls The Manor, which it had already built into the game before the municipal government offered it for viewing. “When we visited, we’d already made the manor in our game, and when we opened the door, we just went ‘It’s the same!'”

The philosophy behind it is that an office “shouldn’t feel like coming to an office, it should feel like entering a house where you’re just making games with friends.” The team says staying small keeps a strong creative vision and ensures “everything we produce has a real reason to be.” Expedition 33 was a long project, six years for Broche, five and a half for Guillermin and between four and five for most of the team, which is part of why they now want to “let ourselves dream again and be creative again.”

Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 is available on PC, PS5 and Xbox Series X/S, and any Switch 2 version remains unannounced.

items.title: Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 developer would love to bring game to Switch 2, but ‘it’s too early for us to announce anything’
items.summary: In a new interview with Automaton about the inspiration behind its hit turn-based RPG, Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 developer Sandfall Interactive was asked
items.content:
In a new interview with Automaton about the inspiration behind its hit turn-based RPG, Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 developer Sandfall Interactive was asked about the potential for the game to hit Switch 2 in the future. Answering questions were Guillaume Broche, the game’s director, Tom Guillermin, CTO and co-founder of Sandfall, Alan Reynaud, lead character artist, and Alexandre Breton, lead technical artist at Sandfall. The official company stance? “It’s too early for us to announce anything.”

The majority of the interview focuses on how Sandfall believes limitations are what bring out the best aspects of game design. Naturally, this segued into a discussion about the Switch 2, which has more limited hardware specifications compared against the PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X. Answering the question about a Switch 2 port directly, Broche commented, “We are interested in looking for a way to do it, but it’s too early for us to announce anything at this point.”

Elaborating further, Guillermin added, “It’s a big technical challenge because we tried to do something beautiful with the game, but of course, the Switch 2 is not as powerful as the PlayStation or the Xbox Series X. So, it’s an important thing for us to consider, especially given the size of our studio.” Broche mentions that “A lot of features [of Unreal Engine 5] don’t work on Switch 2.”

If you’ve been following the development of Unreal Engine 5, you’ll know that Epic Games has introduced some new features which are aimed specifically at Switch 2 development. As Reynaud brings up, “They’re [Epic Games] introducing features like Lumen Lite now, which is easier to run than the standard Lumen, but these things take time to roll out, so we’ll have to consider the updates coming from Unreal Engine to determine what to do.” Backporting that into Clair Obscur would be a bigger task than simply flicking a switch and being set.

All things considered, it doesn’t seem like Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 will be hitting the Switch 2 anytime soon. While Sandfall probably doesn’t want to overlook the opportunity to bring its game to a wider audience, it might not be technologically feasible given how integral UE5 features were to the game’s look and design.

Peter has been a freelance gaming and film critic for over seven years. His passion for Nintendo is only matched by the size of his collection.

items.title: Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 Studio is “Going to Go a Bit Crazy” With its Next Game, Says CEO
items.summary: In an interview, Guillaume Broche also spoke about how how limitations on developers helps to breed creativity in their games.
items.content:
Following the massive success seen by Sandfall Interactive with last year’s Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 , the studio is now looking to the future. In an interview with Automaton Media , studio CEO Guillaume Broche even said that the team might “go a bit crazy” with its next title. However, it also comes down to the fact that the team wants to “find this flame” that it had for Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 again.

“It’s too early to say anything precise, but we had a lot of fun creating Expedition 33 , and it’s a game that we all love internally, so we want to find this flame, this passion again for the next project,” said Broche on the subject of Sandfall’s next game.

“ Expedition 33 was quite a long project too. Especially for me, it was six years. For Tom it was five and a half, and for most of the other members it was between four and five years. That’s also why we want to let ourselves dream again and be creative again. We’re going to go a bit crazy.”

In the same interview, Broche also reiterated how he doesn’t want the studio to get too big. Noting that there are around 26 employees at Sandfall Interactive right now, Broche spoke about how this means that there are “more than enough people for the pre-production of our next project and the things we want to accomplish.” However, he also said that the limitations of a smaller headcount are good for the team.

“When you have more money, it’s very easy to just bring a lot of people and say ‘We need to make it bigger and bigger!’ and ‘We’re going to fix every single little pain point we had in Expedition 33 .’ But I think that’s a big mistake because limitations are what breed creativity. If we know we can’t do everything, we have to focus on what matters, and I think that philosophy is what made Expedition 33 what it is. It feels very focused; everything has a purpose, and everything is made for a reason. It doesn’t feel like something too big for its own good.”

“That’s why we want to stay small, keep a very strong creative vision, and make sure that everything we produce has a real reason to be.”

Previously, Broche had said that he would also be fine if the studio’s next game wasn’t as successful as Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 . “I don’t really care,” he said. “It’s weird to say, but we didn’t make the first game to please anyone. And I think that’s why it worked.”

“Whether people follow us or not is their decision. But that’s how we see the future.”

Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 was released on PC, PS5, and Xbox Series X/S last year, and has since seen plenty of critical and commercial success. Along with winning several awards, the title has also managed to sell 8 million copies as of April this year. The milestone also happened to coincide with the game’s first anniversary, which saw the release of a free update with additional hairstyles.

items.title: Unreal Engine 5 Made Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 Possible, Yet It Makes A Nintendo Switch 2 Port A Big Challenge
items.summary: Sandfall Interactive reveals how Unreal Engine 5 made Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 possible, but also how it makes a Switch 2 port challenging
items.content:
Since its launch in 2022, Unreal Engine 5 has been one of the most controversial game engines from Epic Games , mostly due to how demanding it is on PlayStation 5 , Xbox Series X , and PC , as well as the performance issues it brings. Although the engine has been significantly improved since , public perception hasn't changed much, with many gamers considering it one of the worst things to happen to modern gaming. However, many developers don't share this sentiment, as Sandfall Interactive , the studio behind the 2025 Game of the Year Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 , couldn't have made the game without it.

"For starters, Unreal Engine has all the tools you need to make a game that looks big, even if you’re not a big team," Sandfall Interactive CEO and Creative Director Guillaume Broche said to Automaton . "And we were very lucky with the release timing of some of Unreal’s newer tools. Unreal Engine 5 itself came at the right time in production, then MetaHuman came at the right time, and so did Nanite and Lumen – everything came at the right time. So we were very lucky with that."

The best thing about Unreal Engine 5 is that it gives developers all the tools they need to make something great, Broche continued, while heaping praise on Blueprints , the visual scripting system that will eventually be deprecated in Unreal Engine 6 , once the new Verse/Scene Graph framework matures. "Blueprints, especially, are very important. Blueprints are like a visual scripting method that allows pretty much anybody in the team to write code thanks to how easy it is. It’s like chaining blocks together. In our studio, we have four programmers, but every game designer and every technical artist uses Blueprints to make game logic or environment logic, and that’s crucial for us to be able to ship this kind of game and this kind of quality."

Technical Artist Alexandre Breton also had only praise for Unreal Engine 5's Blueprints . "Blueprints are part of an ecosystem. It’s visual scripting, so it’s very ludic and you can learn it very easily. It’s part of an ecosystem because a lot of people are using it and sharing content, so you can also find resources like tutorials everywhere. You can also find Blueprint Packs and learn from them. People give them away for free or sell them, and it’s never too expensive. Overall, it’s a system that’s very cool to use."

Although several games powered by Unreal Engine 5 have made their way onto the Nintendo Switch 2 , Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 has yet to do so. The team is interested in a port, but there are technical challenges that are even more daunting for a small studio like Sandfall Interactive .

"It’s a big technical challenge because we tried to do something beautiful with the game, but of course, the Switch 2 is not as powerful as the PlayStation or the Xbox Series X. So, it’s an important thing for us to consider, especially given the size of our studio," said studio Co-founder and CTO Tom Guillermin .

While some Unreal Engine 5 features don't work on Nintendo Switch 2 , which we have known for a while, Lumen Lite could make the port slightly less challenging. "They’re introducing features like Lumen Lite now, which is easier to run than the standard Lumen, but these things take time to roll out, so we’ll have to consider the updates coming from Unreal Engine to determine what to do," said Lead Character and Concept Artist Alan Reynaud .

Considering the high quality of Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 , it would be a shame if Nintendo Switch 2 owners would never get to experience it. At the same time, it's understandable how Sandfall Interactive sees the port as a challenge, given the studio's small size. The current generation Nintendo system has already seen some impressive ports like Cyberpunk 2077 and the Final Fantasy VII Remake series, but they were handled by much bigger studios with developers and resources to invest.

Hopefully Lumen Lite , which has been created specifically for handhelds like the Nintendo Switch 2 , will help this port become a reality.

items.title: Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 Director Says End Of Physical Discs Is ‘Super Sad’
items.summary: The devs also revealed that their publisher discussed skipping physical, but figured players would want to 'hold it in their hands'
items.content:
Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 Physical Games PS5 Sandfall

Earlier this month, PlayStation announced that it would end production of physical video game discs in a few years . This led to a lot of shouting, calls to boycott the company, and more. And the devs behind last year’s hit game Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 recently explained that while they understand the “business” reasons for the decision, it is still “a shame” that discs are going away.

In a new interview with Automaton , as part of a larger post-mortem event, some devs from Clair Obscur studio Sandfall talked about last year’s indie (?) super hit . But the team was also asked about the recent news that PlayStation was ending physical disc production of new video games starting in 2028. For them, it’s sad news as they find physical games to be “special” and important to players.

“Personally, I find it super sad because I really like video game stores,” said creative director Guillaume Broche. “And even if nowadays, I play mainly on PC myself, we have a lot of people on the team who play on PS5 and love to collect physical discs. I think it’s part of the beauty of art too—that it’s something tangible that you can touch. I completely appreciate that people want to have their rows of DVDs and games and just feel that they own them. So I think it’s a shame.”

Broche added that while it makes sense “business-wise,” in terms of the “artistry of video games, it’s a sad decision.”

Sandfall co-founder and CTO Tom Guillermin shared an interesting story regarding Expedition 33 ‘s own physical edition. Before the release of the game, there were discussions about not doing a physical release. Physical releases add more complications to the process of making and selling a video game, and cutting it can save a lot of money. But for Sandfall, it sounds like it was never a real option. Guillermin said that “physical was something special” for the studio, and that the team wanted players to be able to “hold [the game] in their hands.”

“So even though it made things harder and meant less money per unit,” said Guillermin, “it was important for us to provide players who want to have the physical game in their hands with an option. Because that’s what we value as players too.”

The devs also shared that walking into a store and seeing physical copies of their game made it feel “real.” And that was true of other games, not just their own.

“Knowing that may not be possible again makes me a bit sad,” said lead character and concept artist Alan Reynaud. “And maybe it’s the child in me, but I like to go outside, buy a game, and come back home with it. It’s a nice feeling.”

“ I think the same principle can apply to manga. It’s nice to read on your phone and stuff, but having a real book is just a different feeling. And I don’t think we could imagine a world where manga is just scanned and stored on your computer. It would be sad to not have it in your library. I think the same applies for games. Sure, it makes more sense business-wise, but you lose the spirit of it.”

The Sandfall team isn’t alone in their love of physical media and their concerns for what it could mean for the future. But it seems extremely unlikely that Sony changes its plans at this point, especially when you consider how few physical games are sold compared to digital. The all-digital future is coming , and unfortunately it doesn’t seem like Sony or Xbox are ready for it. You can read more of Automaton ‘s interview with the Expedition 33 team here.

items.title: "It's a sad decision." Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 developers on the end of physical disc production and why they pushed for a physical release despite the drawbacks
items.summary: Interview with Sandfall Interactive's core members about what physical games mean to them.
items.content:
Home Interviews “It’s a sad decision.” Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 developers on the end of physical disc production and why they pushed for a physical release despite the drawbacks Interview with Sandfall Interactive's core members about what physical games mean to them.

Interviews 2026-07-29 00:01 Genki 1 Epic Games Japan and Sandfall Interactive recently hosted a Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 postmortem event in Yokohama, Japan, where the developers shared technical insights into the making of 2025’s Game of the Year. Following the event, AUTOMATON sat down with the team and took the opportunity to ask about their thoughts on physical game releases. With PlayStation set to end game disc production in 2028, the developers briefly reflected on why they insisted on releasing Expedition 33 physically despite the added challenges, and discussed why they believe physical editions remain important to video games as a medium.

Guillaume Broche – Sandfall Interactive CEO and Creative Director Tom Guillermin – Sandfall Interactive Co-founder and CTO Alan Reynaud – Lead Character and Concept Artist Alexandre Breton – Technical Artist

For more about Sandfall Interactive’s Japanese influences, thoughts on Unreal Engine, and studio upsizing, check out part one of this interview .

— PlayStation recently announced that it will end physical disk production in 2028. What are your thoughts on that?

Guillaume Broche: Personally, I find it super sad because I really like video game stores. And even if nowadays, I play mainly on PC myself, we have a lot of people on the team who play on PS5 and love to collect physical discs. I think it’s part of the beauty of art too – that it’s something tangible that you can touch. I completely appreciate that people want to have their rows of DVDs and games and just feel that they own them. So I think it’s a shame. I mean, business-wise, I can understand why it may make sense, but I think in terms of the artistry of video games, it’s a sad decision.

Tom Guillermin: In our discussions with our publisher prior to the release of Expedition 33, the question of whether or not to do a physical release cropped up. A physical release adds more constraints because you have to account for the production time of the physical items, and you also earn less money per copy.

But for us, physical was something special. We also felt that the game could be special to players, and that they would want to, as Guillaume said, hold it in their hands.

So even though it made things harder and meant less money per unit, it was important for us to provide players who want to have the physical game in their hands with an option. Because that’s what we value as players too.

Guillaume Broche: To add to that, there were two very strong moments when the game released. After launch, we went to a video game store to buy our own game (laughs). Just as a gesture. And another strong memory I have is when someone from Japan sent me a picture [of our game] from a video game store – in Akihabara I think – in Japanese writing and all. I felt like a kid when I saw it. I was like “Yeah, it’s real!” It starts feeling real when you see it in stores. Alan Reynaud: Even now when I’m going to the supermarket or something, if I see our game in a store, it always makes my day. It’s a bit selfish, because it’s our game, but it always makes me go “Oh!”

Knowing that may not be possible again makes me a bit sad. And maybe it’s the child in me, but I like to go outside, buy a game, and come back home with it. It’s a nice feeling.

Alexandre Breton: And it’s not just because it’s “our game.” I think what’s cool [about physical games in general] is that a few years later, you’ll have your box, and you can hold it and look at the title and remember all the memories that are linked to the game.

Alan Reynaud: I think the same principle can apply to manga. It’s nice to read on your phone and stuff, but having a real book is just a different feeling. And I don’t think we could imagine a world where manga is just scanned and stored on your computer. It would be sad to not have it in your library. I think the same applies for games. Sure, it makes more sense business-wise, but you lose the spirit of it.

Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 is available for PC ( Steam ), PS5 and Xbox Series X|S.

items.title: 'Clair Obscur: Expedition 33' stripped of Indie Game Awards due to generative AI use
items.summary: It had previously been announced Game of the Year.
items.content:
The Indie Game Awards has stripped Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 of both its Game of the Year and Debut Game awards, citing the roleplaying game's use of generative AI.

Run by Six One Indie , the annual Indie Game Awards aims to highlight excellence in independent video game development. Titles are eligible for consideration in the Indie Game Awards if their developers are outside the "traditional publisher system," and were not owned or financially controlled by a major corporation. Said games also must not have used any generative AI in their development process, which would make them "strictly ineligible for nomination."

Unfortunately, it appears that Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 's developer Sandfall Interactive did indeed use generative AI, disqualifying them from the Indie Game Awards.

"The Indie Game Awards have a hard stance on the use of gen AI throughout the nomination process and during the ceremony itself," the Indie Game Awards wrote, announcing its decision over the weekend. "When it was submitted for consideration, a representative of Sandfall Interactive agreed that no gen AI was used in the development of Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 .

"In light of Sandfall Interactive confirming the use of gen AI art in production on the day of the Indie Game Awards 2025 premiere, this does disqualify Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 from its nomination. While the assets in question were patched out and it is a wonderful game, it does go against the regulations we have in place."

The Indie Game Awards' Game of the Year and Debut Game will now be awarded to the second-highest scoring titles in each respective category. As such, Debut Game goes to à la mode games ' survival horror Sorry We’re Closed , while the Indie Game Awards' Game of the Year 2025 is Dogubomb 's puzzle adventure game Blue Prince .

The IGAs Nomination Committee is officially retracting Debut Game and Game of the Year, awarding both categories to new recipients. Additionally, we are retracting one of the Indie Vanguard recipients. Full details can be found in our FAQ under Game Eligibility: www.indiegameawards.gg/faq [image or embed]

Sandfall Interactive had previously disclosed its use of AI in a July interview with Spanish newspaper El País , though did not explicitly confirm that the tools they used were generative in nature. At the time, Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 's producer François Meurisse merely stated that they had used "some AI" in the game's production.

In a later update to El País ' article, Sandfall Interactive claimed that no generative AI assets currently remain in Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 . However, it confirmed that generative AI was used to create placeholder textures during development, not all of which were removed prior to release due to oversights in the quality assurance process. Sandfall Interactive states that such AI-generated textures were replaced within five days of Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 's launch, and were never intended to be included in the final game.

Players did indeed spot AI-generated textures in Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 upon its April 24 release, quickly calling out suspicious in-game posters on social media . Less than a week later, patch notes for a hotfix noted that the developers had "replaced a placeholder texture with the correct visual asset."

Even so, the Indie Game Awards were apparently unaware of these events, as it did not discover Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 's AI use until Dec. 18, the day the winners were announced.

Reaction to Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 's disqualification from the Indie Game Awards has been mixed. While some fans appreciate the awards' strict stance against generative AI, others feel that Sandfall Interactive's use of the technology to create a few placeholder poster assets was relatively minor and should be permissible in this case. Still, the Indie Game Awards' criteria requires that no generative AI be used at all, regardless of the extent of such use.

"Thank you for standing up and speaking out for a more ethical games industry," wrote @erin-hallow on Bluesky. "In a time where authentic human creativity is under threat and big players perpetuate that issue, it means a lot to see an awards show that truly cares about the authenticity of the games it showcases."

"Considering a single placeholder asset made it into the final version, entirely by mistake, it seems a bit silly but rules are rules I guess," Redditor u/Caridor wrote on the r/expedition33 subreddit . (Note: Technically at least two placeholder assets were spotted, but their sentiment stands. )

items.title: Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 is now available in Arabic!
items.summary: Expeditioners! Following the huge demand from so many of you, we’ve been working super hard to be able to finally announce that Clair Obscur: Expedition 33, is now available with Arabic text! This brings the total number of supported langua
items.content:
Expeditioners!

Following the huge demand from so many of you, we’ve been working super hard to be able to finally announce that Clair Obscur: Expedition 33, is now available with Arabic text!

This brings the total number of supported languages to 20!

With the new Arabic language support, we had to consider additional changes to the game’s UI to ensure a smooth and enjoyable experience for Arabic-speaking players around the world.

Adding Arabic localization has been a true team effort over many months, from the incredible adaptation and localization work carried out by the linguists, to reworking the vast majority of the user interface for right-to-left reading, all the way through localization testing.

Every team involved brought passion and dedication to making this possible, and we couldn’t be more grateful for their work. We hope this update makes the story feel even more personal to our players.

Today’s update also includes some additional fixes and improvements. Read the full patch notes here!

Thank you all so much for your continued support! <3

Tomorrow comes.

~ The Expedition 33 Team

items.title: 1st Anniversary of Clair Obscur: Expedition 33
items.summary: Expeditioners!! Today marks 1 year since we released Clair Obscur: Expedition 33. This past year has been an incredible journey and so we have a few things to share with you today. To celebrate the occasion, the team put together a special
items.content:
Expeditioners!! 

 

Today marks 1 year since we released Clair Obscur: Expedition 33. This past year has been an incredible journey and so we have a few things to share with you today. 

 

To celebrate the occasion, the team put together a special piece of artwork that we hope you will enjoy! 

8 Million Copies Sold

We're so thrilled, and honestly still quite overwhelmed, to announce that Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 has officially reached 8 million copies sold!

Thank you so so much to every single person who has played, created art, shared, streamed, discussed, and supported this game!!

Game Update: New Haircuts + Patch Notes

We've pushed a fun little update live today: new haircuts are now available in-game, giving the expedition even more style to strut around in! 💅 

For the full list of changes, fixes, and improvements, you can read the patch notes here

Community Emotes

Our community is packed with phenomenally talented artists and we wanted to celebrate that today.  

We commissioned some of our amazing community creators to design official Expedition 33 emotes for you to use in your own channels! 

A massive thank you to IrunoArt, comickergirl (Sarah Leuver), and Bugyakis for their brilliant work on each of these!!

They're FREE to download and use here

Official Baguette Merch

In the mood to add some baguette to your wardrobe? 

We’ve partnered with Orcival and Le Béret Français to bring you the official Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 striped shirt and beret for your cosplays! 🥖    You can purchase the official Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 x Orcival mariniere here

And the official Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 x Le Béret Français beret is available to buy here

On top of that, keep an eye out for a limited number of units of the Monolith Set to be back in stock from our partners at Laced and Pix n' Love soon!! 

And Finally… Cake

It's been a big day for us. Thank you for making it possible. 🎂 

And if you know someone who wants to pick up the game, we're running a 20% sale right now on Steam - As well as some fun merchandise goodies available on our merch page!

Merch Page

From the bottom of our hearts, we’re so thankful to each and every one of you – this has been the best year of our lives, thanks to you. 

 

- The Expedition 33 Team

    [/*]

    [/*]

    [/*]

Environment
